faq.q: What is the best time of day for dolphin watching in Marbella?
faq.a: The best time is early morning (08:00-10:00) when seas are calm and dolphins feed near the surface. Late afternoon (16:00-18:00) also offers good sightings as dolphins become active again before dusk. Both windows provide excellent visibility and comfortable temperatures.

faq.q: Are afternoon dolphin tours better than morning ones?
faq.a: It depends on your preferences. Morning tours offer calmer seas and cooler weather, ideal for families. Afternoon tours often include sunset views and warmer water, which can increase dolphin surface activity. Both times have high sighting success rates in Marbella.

faq.q: What dolphins can we see on a Marbella boat tour?
faq.a: The most common species are common bottlenose dolphins and striped dolphins. Occasionally, you may spot Risso's dolphins or even pilot whales. Sightings are frequent along the Costa del Sol, especially near Cabopino and the protected waters of the Alboran Sea.

faq.q: How long does a dolphin watching tour from Puerto Banús last?
faq.a: Most dolphin watching tours last 2-4 hours. Morning tours are typically 2-3 hours, while afternoon tours can extend to 4-6 hours to include sunset. Our boats like the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are perfect for these durations.

faq.q: What is included in a dolphin watching charter from Boat Rental Marbella?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Just bring sunscreen and your camera.

faq.q: Can we swim with dolphins on these tours?
faq.a: No, swimming with dolphins is not permitted on our tours. We follow responsible wildlife viewing guidelines to avoid disturbing the animals. You can observe them from the boat, which offers excellent photo opportunities.

faq.q: What is the best month for dolphin watching in Marbella in 2048?
faq.a: May through October are the best months, with peak sightings in June and September when water temperatures are warmest. In 2048, we expect similar patterns. Book early for these months as charters fill quickly.

data.body_html:
Marbella dolphin watching in 2048 offers unforgettable encounters with wild dolphins along the Costa del Sol. The best time to book your tour depends on whether you prefer calm morning seas or warm afternoon waters. This guide compares morning vs afternoon boat tours from Puerto Banús, so you can choose the perfect window for your charter.

Why timing matters for dolphin sightings

Dolphins are most active during feeding times, typically at dawn and dusk. In Marbella, this means early morning (08:00-10:00) and late afternoon (16:00-18:00) offer the highest chance of sightings. Water temperature also plays a role: warmer afternoons can increase surface activity, while cooler mornings keep dolphins closer to shore. Our skippers know these patterns intimately and adjust routes accordingly.

Morning dolphin tours: calm seas, cooler air

Morning tours depart Puerto Banús between 08:00 and 10:00. The sea is usually flat, with light winds and temperatures around 22-26°C in summer. This is ideal for families with young children or anyone prone to seasickness. Dolphins are often spotted feeding near the surface, making them easy to photograph. Our Boat Rental Marbella fleet includes the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax), both perfect for 2-3 hour morning trips at €749 for 2 hours.

Afternoon dolphin tours: warmer water, sunset views

Afternoon tours start from 14:00 onwards, often extending into sunset. Water temperatures peak at 24-28°C, which can stimulate dolphin activity. You’ll also enjoy golden hour light for stunning photos. Tours can last 4-6 hours, combining dolphin watching with swimming stops at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. Larger groups might prefer the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) at €4,719 for 4 hours, which includes a free jet ski.

What to expect on your dolphin watching charter

All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% VAT. You just need sunscreen, a hat, and a camera. Dolphins are wild animals, but sighting success rates exceed 90% in the Alboran Sea, especially near Cabopino and the mouth of the Río Verde.

Best boats for dolphin watching

For small groups (up to 5 pax), the Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) offer intimate experiences. Medium groups (6-10 pax) fit well on the Pershing 46 (14m) or Fairline Targa 12m (12m). Large parties (up to 12 pax) can book the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) or Ferretti 94 (29m). All depart from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella’s marina.
